Description: explicit — color-relief exists on MapLibre Native
prompt: Android, MapLibre Native (Kotlin). I have Terrarium-encoded DEM tiles and I want elevation-banded color under my vector layers — green lowlands through brown to white peaks, with the breakpoints in the style so our cartographer can tune them. Can I do that in a MapLibre Android app, or do I have to pre-render colored raster tiles and ship those instead?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
**Short answer:**  
Yes – you can colour-band a Terrarium-encoded DEM directly in a MapLibre Android app.  
All you need is a **`raster-dem` source** that points at your Terrarium tiles and a **`color-relief` layer** that uses an `["interpolate", …, ["elevation"], …]` expression.  
The feature has been part of MapLibre Native since **android-v13.0.0** (and iOS v6.24.0). If you are on an older release you must upgrade or fall back to pre-rendered raster tiles.

Below is a complete, copy-and-paste-ready guide:

---

## 1️⃣ Prerequisites

| What you need | Minimum version |
|---------------|-----------------|
| MapLibre Android SDK | **13.0.0** (released 2025-09-03) |
| Terrarium-encoded DEM tiles (z/x/y.png) | – |
| Kotlin 1.6+ (or Java) | – |

If you are still on, say, `android-v12.x.x`, upgrade the SDK in your `build.gradle`:

```gradle
implementation "org.maplibre.gl:android-sdk:13.0.0"
```

(Or a newer version – the latest stable is always safe.)

---

## 2️⃣ The style JSON (the “declarative” way)

You can keep the whole thing in a style file and just load it with `MapView.getMapAsync { … }`.  
Only the two parts that matter are shown here:

```json
{
  "version": 8,
  "sources": {
    "dem": {
      "type": "raster-dem",
      "url": "https://my.cdn.com/terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png",
      "tileSize": 256,
      "encoding": "terrarium",          // <-- tells MapLibre the Terrarium format
      "maxzoom": 14
    }
  },

  "layers": [
    {
      "id": "relief",
      "type": "color-relief",
      "source": "dem",
      "paint": {
        "color-relief-color": [
          "interpolate",
          ["linear"],
          ["elevation"],               // the DEM value at the pixel
          0,   "#2e8b57",              // low-land green
          500, "#6b8e23",
          1500, "#8b5a2b",             // mid-range brown
          2500, "#c2b280",
          3500, "#e5e5e5",
          4500, "#ffffff"              // snow-white peaks
        ]
      }
    },

    // …your vector layers go here, placed *above* the relief layer
    {
      "id": "roads",
      "type": "line",
      "source": "my-vector-source",
      "source-layer": "road",
      "paint": { "line-color": "#000", "line-width": 2 }
    }
  ]
}
```

*Why it works*  

* `raster-dem` + `"encoding":"terrarium"` tells the native renderer to decode the 16-bit Terrarium PNGs into real metres.  
* `color-relief` is a raster layer that reads the **`["elevation"]`** expression (built-in) and maps it to colours via any `interpolate` ramp you like.  
* Because the layer is a **raster** layer, it sits *under* your vector layers automatically – just order it before the vector layers in the `layers` array.

---

## 3️⃣ Adding the same thing programmatically (Kotlin)

If you prefer to build the style in code (e.g. you need to switch DEM archives at runtime), the API mirrors the JSON exactly.

```kotlin
import org.maplibre.android.maps.Style
import org.maplibre.android.style.sources.RasterDemSource
import org.maplibre.android.style.layers.ColorReliefLayer
import org.maplibre.android.style.expressions.Expression
import org.maplibre.android.style.expressions.Expression.*

mapView.getMapAsync { mapboxMap ->
    mapboxMap.setStyle(Style.Builder()) { style ->

        // 1️⃣ Add the Terrarium DEM source
        val demSource = RasterDemSource(
            "dem",
            "https://my.cdn.com/terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png",
            256
        ).apply {
            // Terrarium is the default for raster-dem, but being explicit never hurts
            setEncoding("terrarium")
            maxZoom = 14
        }
        style.addSource(demSource)

        // 2️⃣ Add the colour-relief layer
        val reliefLayer = ColorReliefLayer("relief", "dem").withProperties(
            PropertyFactory.colorReliefColor(
                // The same interpolate ramp as in the JSON example
                raw(
                    """["interpolate",
                       ["linear"],
                       ["elevation"],
                       0,   "#2e8b57",
                       500, "#6b8e23",
                       1500, "#8b5a2b",
                       2500, "#c2b280",
                       3500, "#e5e5e5",
                       4500, "#ffffff"]"""
                )
            )
        )
        // Insert it before any vector layers you will add later
        style.addLayerBelow(reliefLayer, "water")   // or any existing layer id

        // 3️⃣ Add your vector source / layers as usual …
        // style.addSource(...)
        // style.addLayer(...)
    }
}
```

**Key points in the code**

* `RasterDemSource` → `setEncoding("terrarium")`.  
* `ColorReliefLayer` → `PropertyFactory.colorReliefColor(...)`.  
* The colour ramp is supplied via `Expression.raw()` (or `Expression.literal()` if you prefer building it piece-by-piece).  
* The layer must be added **below** the vector layers you want to appear on top.

---

## 4️⃣ How the cartographer can tune the break-points

Because the colour ramp lives in the style JSON (or in the `Expression.raw` string), the cartographer can edit it without touching any Kotlin code:

```json
"color-relief-color": [
  "interpolate",
  ["linear"],
  ["elevation"],
  0,   "#2e8b57",
  800, "#6b8e23",
  1800, "#8b5a2b",
  2800, "#c2b280",
  3800, "#e5e5e5",
  4800, "#ffffff"
]
```

*Just change the numbers or colours, rebuild the style file (or reload it from the server), and the app will instantly reflect the new banding.*

If you need a UI inside the app to let a user slide break-points, you can rebuild the `Expression.raw` string at runtime and call `reliefLayer.setProperties(...)` again – the renderer updates instantly.

---

## 5️⃣ What to do if you are on an older SDK

| SDK version | What you’ll see | Work-around |
|-------------|----------------|------------|
| `< 13.0.0`  | The `color-relief` layer is ignored (the whole layer is dropped, no crash). | Upgrade to at least **13.0.0**. If you cannot upgrade, pre-render coloured raster tiles (e.g. using GDAL or Mapbox-style-tools) and serve them as a normal `raster` source. |
| `< 13.7.1`  | `interpolate-hcl` / `interpolate-lab` are unavailable (they would cause the layer to be dropped). | Use a plain `["interpolate", ["linear"], …]` ramp with enough intermediate stops – the visual result is the same, just in sRGB space. |

---

## 6️⃣ TL;DR checklist

1. **Upgrade** to `org.maplibre.gl:android-sdk:13.0.0` (or newer).  
2. Add a **`raster-dem` source** with `"encoding":"terrarium"`.  
3. Add a **`color-relief` layer** that references that source.  
4. Supply the colour ramp via an `["interpolate", ["linear"], ["elevation"], …]` expression – the cartographer can edit the numbers in the style JSON.  
5. Place the `color-relief` layer **below** your vector layers.  

That’s it – no need to pre-render coloured raster tiles, no extra server, and the colour bands are fully controllable from the style. Happy mapping!

| Feature | GL JS | MapLibre Native (Android) | Gap closed in |
|---------|------|---------------------------|---------------|

So the only thing you have to watch is the **minimum native version**. Anything older will simply drop the `color-relief` layer (you’ll see a log line like `[ParseStyle]: value must be a string` and the layer disappears).

*What you can tweak:*  
- **Break-points** (`0, 500, 1500 …`) are the exact numbers your cartographer will adjust.  
- **Colours** are any CSS hex strings (or `rgba()`).  
- If you prefer perceptual colour ramps, replace `["linear"]` with `["interpolate-hcl"]` or `["interpolate-lab"]` – those work on Android v13.7.1+.

## 3️⃣ Adding the same thing from Kotlin (if you prefer code)

If you generate the style at runtime or want to add the layer programmatically, the API mirrors the JSON exactly.

```kotlin
import org.maplibre.android.maps.Style
import org.maplibre.android.style.layers.ColorReliefLayer
import org.maplibre.android.style.sources.RasterDemSource
import org.maplibre.android.style.expressions.Expression
import org.maplibre.android.style.expressions.Expression.*

mapView.getMapAsync { mapboxMap ->
    mapboxMap.setStyle(
        Style.Builder()
            .fromUri("asset://my-base-style.json")   // or a remote URL
            .withSource(
                RasterDemSource("dem") {
                    url("https://my.cdn.com/terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png")
                    tileSize(256)
                    encoding("terrarium")
                    maxzoom(14)
                }
            )
            .withLayer(
                ColorReliefLayer("relief", "dem").withProperties(
                    PropertyFactory.colorReliefColor(
                        raw(
                            """[
                              "interpolate","linear",
                              ["elevation"],
                              0,"#2e8b57",
                              500,"#6abf40",
                              1500,"#b5a642",
                              2500,"#c28e3c",
                              3500,"#d07c34",
                              4500,"#e0692c",
                              5500,"#ffffff"
                            ]"""
                        )
                    )
                )
            )
    )
}
```

*Key points in the code above*  

| What you’re doing | Native API call | Why it matters |
|-------------------|----------------|----------------|
| Declare a DEM source | `RasterDemSource(...).encoding("terrarium")` | Tells the raster-dem loader to decode Terrarium PNGs (the same as `"encoding":"terrarium"` in JSON). |
| Add a colour-relief layer | `ColorReliefLayer(...).withProperties(PropertyFactory.colorReliefColor(...))` | The only layer type that can read `["elevation"]`. |
| Use `Expression.raw()` (or `raw("""…""")`) | Allows you to paste the exact GL JS expression verbatim, including `["elevation"]`. | Typed builders stop at `interpolate`; `raw` is the simplest way to get the full expression. |
| Place the layer **before** your vector layers | Add the `ColorReliefLayer` first, then add vector layers later (or set its `above`/`below` property). | The colour-relief is drawn *under* everything else, just like a hill-shade background. |

## 4️⃣ What to do if you can’t upgrade to v13.0.0+

*Older native releases (≤ v12.x)* simply **ignore** the `color-relief` layer. The map will still load the DEM (you can still use a `hillshade` layer), but the colour ramp will never appear.

**Work-arounds**

| Option | How it works | Pros | Cons |
|-------|--------------|------|------|
| **Pre-render coloured raster tiles** (e.g. generate PNGs with the same colour ramp on the server) | Treat them as ordinary raster tiles (`type":"raster"`). | Works on any native version. | Requires a build step, larger tile size, no on-the-fly colour tweaking. |
| **Use `hillshade`** (flat shading) | `type":"hillshade"` on the same DEM source. | No extra build step, works on all releases. | Only grayscale shading, no colour bands. |
| **Upgrade** | Bump your Gradle dependency to `implementation "org.maplibre.gl:android-sdk:13.0.0"` (or newer). | Gives you the full `color-relief` feature plus later parity fixes. | May require a small code-base update (e.g., new API signatures). |

If you are already on **android-v13.0.0** (or later) you’re good to go – no extra work needed.

---

## 5️⃣ Quick checklist before you ship

| ✅ Checklist | What to verify |
|--------------|----------------|
| **Native version** | `MapLibre.getVersion()` ≥ 13.0.0 (for `color-relief`). |
| **DEM source** | `"type":"raster-dem"` **and** `"encoding":"terrarium"` (or set `encoding("terrarium")` in Kotlin). |
| **Layer order** | `color-relief` layer is *below* any vector layers that need to be coloured on top. |
| **Expression syntax** | Use `["interpolate", …]` (or `interpolate-hcl/lab` if you’re on ≥ 13.7.1). |
| **Cache / offline** | If you need offline tiles, bundle the DEM as an `asset://` URL and reference it as `pmtiles://asset://…` (supported since android-v13.7.1). |
| **Log check** | Run the app with `Logcat` and look for `[ParseStyle]` warnings – they indicate a dropped layer. |
